We’re moving again next week so I popped a few things in the community hub shop nearby including some embroideries I’ve been working on. This skirt was one of the donations. I had it in my shop for a few weeks and it got a little interest but no buyers. So offloading means a lighter case for moving and less to keep shifting around as we live from the case. I hope it eventually ends up in good hands.
I can now share this copper scratchboard I did in September for my big sister’s birthday, it’s today and it’s not a secret any more. Swipe to see it shine
It’s up. I love this wall paint colour

My latest scratchboard piece- another marigold but smaller since the frame was the size of the card, not the inside measurement. So I cut this card to fit and did a smaller scale interpretation still on copper foil, though. Still far from perfect but our host needs a little love at the mo so this is for her. It’s in a distressed blue wooden frame with a Harris tweed heart from Isle of Lewis and Harris (our host is a wool and knit lover and as I gave this to her she was pulling out her stash of Harris tweed for making a baby jacket). It now hangs in the kitchen/dining room.

Practicing values on scratchboard… I dis the Love in a mist and Rudbeckia first and they seem flat because I didn’t do a lot of shading. The Shasta Daisy has the highlights left behind and the shadow removed. Seems the opposite of what I should be doing. You kind of have to train your brain to remove the shadow and leave the black to stand out as a highlight. When I start it doesn’t make a lot of sense but about half way through it begins to take shape. It’s addictive

Art doesn’t always need a lot of planning, complications or experience. An idea, a new tool or a doodle can lead you anywhere. These are my pieces so far for #tuacsepholey and I’m basically just having fun in @theuglyartclub . Every day I wake up excited to get started and play with an idea that struck while laying nursing my babe in the wee hours haha. My @the_truthbrush gets a new life distressing paper, and bubble wrap gets patched 🤷‍♀️ (dreamy gold scratchboard is new)

Still getting a feel for this. This one started as a flower and then went a bit abstract. Playing with definition and pressure as well as sharp lines and stripes. It’s a doodle, just following the blade, and maybe a wip for another time. It will also glow in the dark, so maybe I’ll have a look at it in darkness later and know for sure.

Recently I’ve been really getting into this scratchboard stuff. The limit on colour and material means I take a lot more care and consideration when I do a piece. The cards come in packs of 6 which means I don’t want to realise at any point it was a mistake. I chose to die this 禅 Chinese character that means Zen, I knew I wanted to remove a larger area this time to try and improve on that, and I have got a much smoother surface this time. It’s all part of getting used to the tool and trying it out. The nature of the material means all the mistakes are on show. This is another glow in the dark piece.
